meaningfulChallengesAndResolution.partnerPoint: A-AUD-3 proposes a brief adjacent verified owner cue for a future attribution stimulus.
meaningfulChallengesAndResolution.challenge: A cropped/scrolled stage lacks heyNag, while the full document supplies the name, biography and project link. Lack of the name in a crop does not prove natural browsing causes misattribution. Adding an owner cue is a testable staging choice, not a validated remedy.
meaningfulChallengesAndResolution.resolution: Keep A’s observation and hypothesis. Record actual viewport, scroll, name/moth visibility and playback exposure. Preserve normal brand/project context when testing owner attribution or recall; use an isolated neutral clip only when testing action comprehension. These answer different questions.

meaningfulChallengesAndResolution.partnerPoint: A-AUD-1 notes near-neighbor held emotions; B-AB3 notes the small presenting mitten’s limited independent specificity.
meaningfulChallengesAndResolution.challenge: Similarity in a labeled static catalogue is not evidence that people confuse the selected actions during playback. Nor does every one of the 24 emotions need unique naming at avatar size.
meaningfulChallengesAndResolution.resolution: Keep the deductions as scoped craft judgments. Prioritize the few contrasts used in an actual product; examine full-size unlabeled stills and continuous clips before changing poses. Preserve tiny anatomy and avoid adding motion or detail merely to increase a score.

meaningfulChallengesAndResolution.partnerPoint: A-AUD-2 notes weaker 32–48px night antenna stem continuity.
meaningfulChallengesAndResolution.challenge: The actual-size proof supports a narrow scale observation, not a general night-identity failure or a measured recognition loss.
meaningfulChallengesAndResolution.resolution: Accept the proposal’s day universal 32px mark and larger night usage. If revisited, compare a tightly scoped edge variant at the exact size before altering larger character paint. No audience recognition claim follows from this choice.

meaningfulChallengesAndResolution.partnerPoint: Both reviews caution that labels prime interpretation.
meaningfulChallengesAndResolution.challenge: Neutral prompts are required for some research questions, but labels are useful and appropriate for the current authoring/selection tool. Removing them globally would weaken the studio and removing brand context from an attribution test would change the question.
meaningfulChallengesAndResolution.resolution: Keep the local labeled studio. For future unprimed action comprehension, make a separate one-direction stimulus and free-response prompt; introduce diagnostic labels only afterward. Keep accessibility and document the modality rather than silently stripping descriptions.

meaningfulChallengesAndResolution.partnerPoint: Both reviews praised improved portrait legibility; v2 explicitly adds the stacked-phone eyeline limitation.
meaningfulChallengesAndResolution.challenge: A larger character is easier to inspect, but the authored screen-right glance is not literal alignment with the upper-right stacked question in every pose.
meaningfulChallengesAndResolution.resolution: Accept v2’s named spatial limitation. Keep it as a future within-anatomy staging/timing hypothesis, not evidence of confused viewers and not a reason to revive the superseded cramped phone layout.

cadenceReconciliation: The newer active-only desktop record reports 119 intervals, mean 34.45ms, p95 35ms, maximum 67ms and four above 50ms. It narrows the technical observation; it neither attributes earlier mixed idle one-second gaps to SVG nor establishes normal-speed experience, GPU cost or phone behavior. My score is unaffected.
remainingDisagreements: Numerical scores remain different and have different narrow emphasis: A 8.2 for static emotional staging/attribution; B 8.3 for visual association/research readiness. This is not a substantive objection.

B treats absence of a neutral research wrapper and matched exposure as readiness deductions, not missing production requirements. A emphasizes static cue and scale compromises. Both accept local use with those distinctions visible.
acceptedJointRecommendation: Keep hypotheses separate from owner preference and expert craft. Audience outcomes remain unscored; authoring labels are not neutral research stimuli.
practicalSkillsWorkflowAgreement: Use the 17-entry catalog for routing, then read relevant complete instructions; both audience reviewers read emil-design-eng, prototype and mobile-native in full.

Name the decision before building a variant: owner personal fit, static craft, action comprehension, name attribution or delayed recall. Prototype divergence must answer that decision, with one realistic full-size direction shown at a time and immediate switching for expert/owner comparison.

Separate the authoring picker from first-exposure research. For research, specify neutral prompts, free-response order and whether randomization/counterbalancing is warranted. For natural branded exposure retain real context and log viewport/scroll, version, theme, duration and playback.
Keep owner choice, craft judgments, source/mechanical checks, human usability observations and memory outcomes in separate fields; an AI consensus or target score fills none of the missing fields.

Future engineers apply immediate accessible UI feedback independently of intentional character playback. Source/capability checks do not graduate into phone, spoken-AT or continuous-motion claims without the relevant evidence.
skillsExceptions: No new prototype or permission pause: owner selection already exists and this is a review. Preserve historical studies despite generic prototype cleanup guidance.
Do not apply sub-300ms UI budgets or no-keyboard-animation rules to intentional Play content.
Do not erase SVG expressive anatomy to satisfy transform/opacity advice; measure the relevant workload.
Do not lock document scroll, zoom or body selection or remove useful link feedback by copying a global mobile baseline.
Do not remove useful authoring labels or accessible descriptions solely to create a research stimulus; use a separate, appropriate exposure design.

personalScore.meaning: Strong, coherent visual association material and unusually clear evidence boundaries; not yet a neutral, exposure-controlled audience research stimulus. Ordinal specialist judgment within this narrow inspected scope, not an empirical success rate.

audienceOutcomes.reason: No unfamiliar human participants or measured memory outcomes. Nag choosing Investigate & share establishes personal fit only.

conclusion: Agree with the exact v2 audience recommendation and implemented local foundation, with named nonblocking limits. No source edits or recruitment requested in this round.
